Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Marco Reyes (VP Eng - Opal), Aisha Malik (Product - Opal), Ben Cho (Infra - Opal), Noah Singh (Data Eng - Opal)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align on pilot goals, network requirements, success metrics, and next steps. Action: Redwood to send pricing and runbook; Opal to share traffic profile and prompts.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Samir at Redwood, i'll kick off real quick. The agenda - introductions, pilot scope, success metrics, infra/network items, then next steps. Lina, want to intro from SE side?
[00:22] Lina: Yep hi all, Lina Park, solutions engineering. i'll be handling the tech onboarding and helping with bench marks and runtime configuration. Sorry for the slightly choppy audio on my side.
[00:33] Marco: Marco here. we're excited—we've been evaluating inference providers and we want to run a small pilot for our customer support assistant. timeline is tight, Q4-ish.
[00:45] Aisha: Hi, Aisha. product lead on the bot. success for us is latency under 600ms for 95% of calls and parity with our current answers on the fallback set.
[00:58] Ben: Ben, infra. i'll own networking and security asks. we use AWS VPC, cross-account peering, and strict egress rules.
[01:12] Samir: Great, that's helpful. Quick qual: is Opal planning hosted (Redwood API) or private (VPC/on-prem)?
[01:20] Marco: We want to start hosted for speed but need VPC/private option for GDPR-sensitive customers in EMEA. So pilot hosted with private-compatible configs is ideal.
[01:33] Lina: makes sense. we usually do hosted pilot then snapshot config for dedicated/private. i'll note the EMEA residency constraint.
[01:41] Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
[01:47] Samir: On the pilot scope — we're proposing a 6-week pilot: week 0 setup, week 1 smoke + perf baseline, weeks 2-4 tuning & evaluation, weeks 5-6 wrap + handoff. Goal is to validate latency, cost-at-scale, and answer quality with your prompt set. Does that fit?
[02:06] Marco: Yes, that maps. Budget wise we have an initial commit for a reserved pool? we need to confirm numbers though.
[02:17] Samir: We'll send a pilot pricing sheet; typical reserved pilot has a small monthly commit and overage protection.
[02:25] Aisha: we also want automatic fallback to smaller models when load spikes, and a canary rollout. is that in scope?
[02:34] Lina: Absolutely — we support routing policies, automatic fallback to compatible model variants and canary rollouts. sometimes docs call it "smart routing" but in the console it's under routing/policies.
[02:47] Noah: are there sample logs / telemetry we get? token-level cost breakdown?
[02:52] Jordan: yes, Console gives token and latency breakdown per-request and you can export traces. We'll share a sample dashboard screenshot in the runbook.
[03:05] Marco: Security questions — SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS?
[03:11] Samir: We are SOC2 compliant, we have ISO in flight; for SSO we support SAML/SCIM and RBAC; and we integrate with customer KMS for Private. Lina will attach our security whitepaper.
[03:24] Ben: for hosted pilot, do you store prompts or logs long-term? our legal team wants short retention and redaction.
[03:33] Lina: Default retention is 30 days for hosted but you can request shorter retention or disable logs. We also have a private mode that avoids storing prompts in the control plane. The auto-transcription sometimes flags product names—apologies—there's a "no-store" toggle for sensitive flows.
[03:51] Aisha: perfect. can we get an NDA addendum for data handling?
[03:56] Samir: yes, we'll route that to legal. Jordan will own that.
[04:05] Marco: on perf—our p95 target is 600ms, p99 under 1.2s. baseline current 4-500ms for short responses but spikes are painful. We do many multi-turn chats with a median context of 1,200 tokens.
[04:24] Lina: ok context length matters—our runtime adapts kernel selection based on sequence length. we'll want sample loads: RPS, median seq len, and KV cache hit expectations.
[04:38] Noah: current average is 4 RPS per instance, peak 80 RPS for the bot across regions. We use 3 shards currently for our backend.
[04:49] Lina: good, pls share the traffic profile in the shared doc. we'll use that to recommend batching and quantization.
[05:00] Ben: about networking — we do cross-account VPC peering plus static egress IPs. do you support NAT or fixed egress?
[05:08] Samir: For Private we do VPC peering; for hosted we provide static egress IPs or a peered connector depending on region. Lina: I'll send the peering checklist.
[05:18] Aisha: what about observability for product managers — can we see per-prompt quality metrics?
[05:24] Jordan: Console has per-route quality monitoring, and we can set up regression alerts tied to your eval prompt sets. We'll include a sample alert config.
[05:36] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[05:44] Marco: costs — approximate unit economics? we care about tokens per user and cost-per-query.
[05:50] Samir: We'll build a cost model based on your traffic profile and target SLO. The Optimize team can propose batching and quantization options to lower unit cost while keeping quality.
[06:03] Aisha: For the success criteria: 95% latency under 600ms, answer parity >= 90% on fallback set, and cost per session under $0.06. we'll use these as the pilot metrics.
[06:17] Samir: Great — we'll formalize that in the SOW.
[06:22] Lina: quick tech deep-dive — model variants: do you have a preferred open model?
[06:27] Marco: We've experimented with Llama-2 variants internally but performance differs. We want Redwood to recommend model and quantization based on our prompts.
[06:37] Lina: ok, we'll run a short model selection test as part of week 1 to evaluate latency and output quality. sometimes the smaller quantized model meets latency and cost targets with minimal quality loss.
[06:49] Ben: encryption at rest — for hosted, is customer-managed KMS supported?
[06:54] Samir: For hosted we support envelope encryption and CMKs for Dedicated/Private. For hosted public customers we can talk about bring-your-own-key on certain plans. I'll note Legal/Comms to follow.
[07:06] Aisha: can we demo the console briefly?
[07:10] Samir: Sure Lina — can you share your screen?
[07:14] Lina: (screen share noises) Showing Console — routes, model pins, rollout page. Keep in mind the recording might blur actual model names.
[07:31] Speaker 3: (unintelligible)
[07:38] Lina: here's the rollout config — canary 10% for 24 hours, automatic rollback on error rate > 3%. routing policies by region and cost tier are here.
[07:52] Marco: neat. the token breakdown view — can we export per-request?
[07:58] Jordan: yes csv export, or export to your observability endpoint.
[08:05] Ben: network checklist — what we need to provide: CIDRs for VPC peering, allowed ports, and a list of static egress IPs if you use them.
[08:15] Lina: exact list will be in the peering doc I'll send. for hosted we usually need open egress to our IPs or set up the connector.
[08:25] Noah: prompts — we'll send a sample of 200 prompts and 50 eval cases. any preferred format?
[08:31] Lina: JSONL with turn history is best. include expected answer and a tolerance note.
[08:38] Aisha: also logging PII redaction — can the pipeline redact?
[08:43] Lina: yes we have redaction hooks and a pre-send filter you can host. For hosted we provide a redaction plugin; for Private you can run it in your VPC.
[08:55] Marco: legal wants retention shorter than 14 days for EU customers. is that doable?
[09:00] Samir: We can set retention to 7 days for pilot with an addendum. we'll follow up.
[09:07] Jordan: i'll drive the contact with legal and send the addendum.
[09:13] Speaker 1: (paper rustle)
[09:18] Samir: Ok — let's map commitments. Lina will publish an onboarding runbook with the peering checklist and console screenshots. Samir sends pricing + SOW draft and legal addendum. Opal provides traffic profile and prompt samples. Jordan will set a weekly sync invite.
[09:33] Aisha: for evaluation, can we get a quality dashboard with human evals mix-in?
[09:38] Jordan: yes we'll include a simple human-in-the-loop tagging flow for the pilot.
[09:44] Ben: about scale — if pilot hits 200 RPS, do you autoscale?
[09:49] Lina: yes, Dedicated has predictable scaling; hosted can burst but we'll set burst capacity and autoscale policy in the pilot config. we'll simulate load.
[09:59] Marco: any red flags we should be aware of?
[10:02] Samir: only typical things — network peering timing, firewall rules, and prompt privacy. Make sure the sample prompts aren't legal-sensitive.
[10:09] Noah: we'll scrub PII before sharing.
[10:13] Aisha: onboarding timeline — when can we start?
[10:17] Samir: If we lock SOW by 2026-10-12, we can start week of 2026-10-19. Jordan: I'll drop a Doodle for syncs and put a tentative pilot kickoff 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC.
[10:31] Marco: sounds good.
[10:34] Samir: Alright — recap of next steps: pricing and SOW, runbook + peering checklist, sample prompts + traffic, legal addendum, schedule kickoff. Any other questions?
[10:48] Ben: one last thing — do you provide a runbook for incident escalation and on-call contacts?
[10:54] Lina: yes, we'll include runbook and escalation matrix with SLO targets.
[10:59] Jordan: and CSM will set weekly syncs and a slack channel for the pilot.
[11:06] Marco: thanks everyone. we'll review and get the artifacts back by next Friday.
[11:12] Samir: great, thanks all — we'll follow up.

End of call.

Notes: occasional transcription mis-reads: "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Dedicate" shown in auto transcript, speaker attributions sometimes generic. Shared artifacts referenced: /links/onboarding-runbook, /links/pilot-pricing, internal-security-whitepaper.pdf.
